# Groups & Summaries {#sec-groups}

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(nycflights13)
```

## Quick Reference

| Use Case                                  | Function              | Example                                                |
|:------------------------------------------|:----------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| Split the data into groups                | `group_by()`          | `mpg |> group_by(class)`                               |
| Collapse each group to one row of results | `summarize()`         | `summarize(avg_hwy = mean(hwy))`                       |
| Count rows per group                      | `n()`                 | `summarize(n = n())`                                   |
| Count rows per group (shortcut)           | `count()` / `tally()` | `mpg |> count(class, sort = TRUE)`                     |
| Find the center                           | `mean()` / `median()` | `summarize(mean_hwy = mean(hwy))`                      |
| Find the spread                           | `sd()` / `IQR()`      | `summarize(sd_hwy = sd(hwy), iqr_hwy = IQR(hwy))`      |
| Find the extremes                         | `min()` / `max()`     | `summarize(min_hwy = min(hwy), max_hwy = max(hwy))`    |
| Find a percentile                         | `quantile()`          | `quantile(hwy, 0.25)`                                  |
| Ignore missing values                     | `na.rm = TRUE`        | `mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE)`                        |
| Get the first or last value               | `first()` / `last()`  | `summarize(first_model = first(model))`                |
| Group by more than one variable           | `group_by(a, b)`      | `group_by(year, month, day)`                           |
| Remove the grouping                       | `ungroup()`           | `... |> ungroup()`                                     |

A full group-and-summarize pipeline:

```{r}
mpg |>
  group_by(class) |>
  summarize(
    avg_hwy = mean(hwy),
    median_hwy = median(hwy),
    n = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(avg_hwy))
```

## Counting: `count()` versus `tally()` versus `n()`

All three count rows:

- `count()` groups and counts in one step
  - Add `sort = TRUE` to sort greatest to least
- `tally()` counts rows in data that is **already grouped** with `group_by()`
- `n()` only works inside `summarize()` or `mutate()`, so it can sit next to other summaries

```{r}
mpg |> count(drv)

# use group_by() before tally()
mpg |>
  group_by(drv) |>
  tally()

# use n() inside summarize(), alongside other summaries
mpg |>
  group_by(drv) |>
  summarize(
    n_cars = n(),
    avg_hwy = mean(hwy)
  )
```

## Worked Example: Most Delayed Departures by NYC Airport

**Question:** Which NYC airport has the longest average departure delay?

**Pseudocode:** group flights by origin airport → average the departure delay in each group (skip `NA`s for cancelled flights) → count flights per group for context → sort, biggest first.

```{r}
#| label: airport-delays
flights |>
  group_by(origin) |>
  summarize(
    avg_dep_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_flights = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(avg_dep_delay))
```

**Answer:** Newark (EWR) has the longest average departure delay at 15.1 minutes, followed by JFK (12.1) and LaGuardia (10.3).
